document_summary: MassLandlords.net article explaining that Massachusetts landlords (lessors) may not charge rental application fees under M.G.L. c. 186 § 15B, while licensed brokers may charge fees under 254 CMR 7.

rules.title: No application fees by landlords (M.G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
rules.requirement: Before a tenancy begins, a lessor may require payment only of first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and a lock fee; application, pet, cleaning and amenity fees are forbidden. Licensed brokers may charge fees if they comply with 254 CMR 7 (written disclosure of fee amount, timing and contingency).
rules.key_value: Landlords may not charge application fees; only first, last, security deposit and locks may be collected
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to lessors (landlords) before the start of a tenancy; a landlord who is also a broker is likely treated as a landlord first (not settled by appellate case law).
rules.exemptions: Licensed brokers may charge fees under 254 CMR 7 if they follow the board of registration's regulations, including a separate bona fide brokerage operation.
rules.quoted_span: It states that prior to the beginning of a tenancy, no lessor may require payment for anything except first, last, security, and locks
rules.extraction_notes: Secondary source (MassLandlords, updated 2025-01-14). Article says the law has been in effect since the 1970s but gives no specific effective date, so effective_date is null. Federal case Perry v. Equity Residential (2014) found up-front application fees unlawful. Requiring applicants to pay a third-party screening service is considered risky.
